{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Clean revenue: remove commas and convert to float
df['revenue'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Filter out refunded orders
completed_only = df[df['status'] == 'completed']

# Remove QA orders (revenue = 999999.99)
real_orders = completed_only[completed_only['revenue'] != 999999.99]

# Check final shape
print(f"Final dataset size: {len(real_orders)} rows")

# Verify channel distribution
print("Channel distribution:")
print(real_orders['channel'].value_counts())

# Verify customer_segment distribution
print("Customer segment distribution:")
print(real_orders['customer_segment'].value_counts())

# Check for converted=1 only, since we want revenue per converted order
converted_only = real_orders[real_orders['converted'] == 1]

# Ensure we're only analyzing converted orders
print(f"Number of converted orders: {len(converted_only)}")

# Now compute average revenue per converted order by channel, stratified by customer_segment
# First, group by channel and customer_segment
avg_revenue_by_channel_segment = converted_only.groupby(['channel', 'customer_segment'])['revenue'].mean().reset_index()

# Display the results
print("Average revenue per converted order by channel and segment:")
print(avg_revenue_by_channel_segment)

# Compute the difference in average revenue between email and paid_search, within each segment
# We'll compute the difference: email - paid_search
# But only if both channels have data in a segment
# Use pivot to make it easier to compare
pivot_table = avg_revenue_by_channel_segment.pivot(index='customer_segment', columns='channel', values='revenue')

# Compute difference: email - paid_search
pivot_table['diff'] = pivot_table['email'] - pivot_table['paid_search']

print("\nDifference (email - paid_search) by segment:")
print(pivot_table[['email', 'paid_search', 'diff']])"}
